title: Three ship binding sites still compare the audited tree directly, so a carried ship interrupted after its push re-audits instead of healing
summary: Since 2026-09-30 three binding checks apply the one rule (auditBindingSatisfied, which re-proves an ADR-0105 identity carry): the pre-commit and post-push tree checks and verifyAuditBinding's predicate-execution check (verifyExecutionTree). Three still compare the audited tree directly: the post-push idempotency gate (native.go:352, auditTree != committedTree), verifyPostPushPredicateEvidence (audit.go:270, landedTree != entry.WorktreeTreeSHA) and the resume-unpushed heal (repair.go:350, headTree != bound; its comment justifies the raw compare for inbox consumption, whose paths a fresh process cannot know, but a carry is ledger-backed and re-provable in a fresh process). All three fail closed, but a carried ship whose tree differs from the audited one by design misses both fast heals after a push and goes HeadMoved into a deep re-audit, the waste the verifyExecutionTree fix removed on the first attempt (architecture review of that fix, MEDIUM-2).
fix: Route each site through auditBindingSatisfied (or its carry rung where consumption cannot apply), keeping each site's own operator-facing message, and prove a carried ship interrupted after its push heals without a re-audit.
acceptance: A carried ship interrupted after its push resumes to shipped without a re-audit (red today)
No binding site in phases/ship compares the audited tree with a held tree except through auditBindingSatisfied
source: console, 2026-09-30 architecture review of the verifyExecutionTree carry fix (MEDIUM-2)
